newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares slide lower with other markets.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares slide lower with other markets.

text.p: Italian stocks slid lower throughout Friday to close sharply down weighed by falls in Wall Street, other European bourses and world bond markets, dealers said.

Trading was generally light in Milan ahead of the weekend and a shortened trading week with the Ferragosto holiday on August 15 in Italy, dealers said. Fiat was off 1.89 percent at 5,917 lire despite new July car registration figures showing it had outperformed the national market.
All-share Mibtel index ended off 1.69 percent at 14,572, the Mib30 blue chip index down 2.08 percent at 21,985 and the Fib30 September contract 3.28 percent lower at 21,965.
Dealers said that the Milan bourse had started slightly firmer but the negative tone to most other market had pulled Italy stocks back in thin trading.

Italian Transport Minister figures showed July new car registrations leap to 246,500 from 160,007 in July 1996, with Fiat outperforming the market with its July deliveries up 57.13 percent to 108,970.
Car research body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) said orders for new cars showed a moderate rise in July over June and expectations for the next quarter saw deliveries holding steady.
Among the blue chips, oil giant ENI slipped 3.13 percent to end at 10,435 lire, Pirelli was 3.41 percent lower at 4,841 lire and Montedison down 2.05 percent at 1,147 lire.
